_about: Moves for slop-lab v2. Merged from six discovery passes (v2/discovery/moves-*.json, human original vs three model defaults on 24 train tasks) and the seed lists (ne-slop-text loop/questionnaire.json, learn/patterns.md). 'expect' = which side the discovery passes saw it on; the metric learns the real weight. Content presence is in 'material', outside the metric.

sentence_moves.def: A sentence or clause that comments on a fact just given: says what it means, why it matters, why it happened, what it leads to, or how to read it, without adding a new fact ('which means...', 'This shows...', 'That is the real cost.', trailing '-ing' clauses like 'ensuring...', 'making it...').
sentence_moves.not: A consequence that brings new information; irony; a generalization about the whole topic (that is 'moral').

sentence_moves.def: The sentence states the overall point, lesson or the writer's position on the whole topic as a general proposition, detached from any specific event or example ('In the end, trust is earned.', 'So the lesson is...', 'Так что...', 'Итого...').
sentence_moves.not: A step inside the argument that follows from a specific fact; a point carried only by a joke, image or irony.

sentence_moves.def: A sentence (or a sentence-opening clause) whose only job is to announce, order or label what comes next, or to talk about the text itself; it carries no fact of its own ('Here is what happened.', 'Start with the people.', 'There is another difference.', 'Let me explain.', 'Устроено это так.', 'In this post I will...').
sentence_moves.not: A transition that also delivers the fact; a heading; a question (that is 'question').

sentence_moves.def: The sentence tags its claim with an opinion frame or a rank/attitude label instead of just making the claim: 'I think', 'I believe', 'my view is', 'my position is', 'the main idea is', 'the trouble is', 'surprisingly', 'the key point', 'I disagree'.
sentence_moves.not: Hedges on a fact ('perhaps half'); a judgment stated flat with no frame; a feeling acted out (exclamation).

sentence_moves.def: The sentence shows the writer as fair, balanced or kind, or tells the reader how to take the writer's words: 'To be fair', 'That is a reasonable view', 'None of this means I am against X', 'That may sound harsh, but', 'and that is worth something', 'and you can get through it', an added reassurance or compliment to the other side.
sentence_moves.not: A plain concession that sets up a rebuttal without a fairness label; a sarcastic concession (that is 'irony').

sentence_moves.def: The sentence or clause names the writer's inner state (proud, grateful, excited, nervous, it stayed with me, I was surprised) in plain words as a report.
sentence_moves.not: A feeling shown only through wording, oath or exclamation (that is 'exclamation'); a feeling that is the event itself in a narrative scene with details.

sentence_moves.def: The sentence tells the reader what to do or how to take the argument: imperatives like 'consider', 'note', 'remember', 'think about', calls to action, invitations, 'if you..., try...', 'I encourage you'.
sentence_moves.not: Instructions that are the genre's content (install steps, how to use a tool); a slogan quoted from someone; rhetorical questions.

sentence_moves.def: A heading or a label-plus-colon that names a section or point with the plain topic term or a generic label ('Rendering:', 'Getting in early', 'The lesson', 'Моя позиция'), rather than with the writer's own image or phrase.
sentence_moves.not: A heading made of the writer's own image, joke or phrase; the header of a list the genre requires.

sentence_moves.def: The sentence is one of three or more consecutive short sentences that each carry one item of a list with the same frame ('It was slow. It was costly. It was fragile.'). Mark every sentence of the run.
sentence_moves.not: A single sentence that lists items (that is 'inventory'); a bulleted list; repetition used for an argument where each sentence adds new reasoning.

sentence_moves.def: A single sentence that lists three or more items (tools, duties, qualities, steps, examples) as a series.
sentence_moves.not: Two items; a list in bullet form where the genre needs it (still mark it if a bullet itself lists three or more items).

sentence_moves.def: A sentence built for its sound in earnest: 'not X but Y', 'X isn't about A, it's about B', a triad, a chiasmus, a neat aphoristic line or a colon reveal ('The answer: ...') that sounds like a quotable slogan, with no irony.
sentence_moves.not: Ironic or joking lines (that is 'irony'); an image from another domain (that is 'outside_image').

sentence_moves.def: A sentence that would fit any writer or any company writing on this topic: it contains no name, number, event, image or claim specific to this writer's case ('Good communication is essential.', 'Every team faces challenges.').
sentence_moves.not: Short connective sentences already marked 'signpost'; a general claim that is clearly this writer's contrarian position.

sentence_moves.def: The writer rates their own (or their team's/company's) qualities or results in evaluative words ('I am a strong communicator', 'our exceptional team', 'we did an outstanding job').
sentence_moves.not: A plain report of what was done with numbers; quoted praise from others.

sentence_moves.def: A casual marker or a staged joke that performs a voice without saying anything: 'honestly', 'to be frank', 'let's be real', 'the joke answer is... the real answer is...', a fake hedge ('I genuinely don't know') that does not express real doubt about a fact.
sentence_moves.not: A real joke built from the text's subject (that is 'irony'); a real admission of doubt about a fact.

sentence_moves.def: The sentence makes its point through an image, analogy, allusion, proverb, quotation or named thing from outside the literal subject (racecar school, checkers vs chess, a fairy tale, another product, a phone network, a film).
sentence_moves.not: Dead idioms with no live picture ('take a step back', 'on track'); comparisons that stay inside the topic.

sentence_moves.def: The sentence says something the writer does not literally mean, or jokes using the subject's own stuff: sarcasm, mock agreement, deadpan, mock-grand or mock-bureaucratic wording, a comic invented name, self-mockery.
sentence_moves.not: Casual tone with no joke; earnest slogans.

sentence_moves.def: The sentence drops into a markedly different register from the surrounding prose: slang, profanity, folksy or crude words, or words deliberately mismatched with the subject ('a gnarly hack', 'damn', 'херня', 'красава').
sentence_moves.not: Ordinary informal but neutral wording ('a lot', 'pretty good').

sentence_moves.def: A question in the writer's own voice, put to the reader or to themselves (rhetorical or answered next), including an imagined reader's question.
sentence_moves.not: Reporting a question someone else asked; headings that are questions.

sentence_moves.def: Someone's words given as direct speech in their own voice (quote marks, a colon, or an imagined speaker talking), including the reader's imagined retort.
sentence_moves.not: Reported speech ('he said that...'); scare quotes around one term; titles.

sentence_moves.def: The writer breaks into the sentence with a parenthetical or dashed comment (an afterthought, a reaction, a joke, a credit, 'so to speak', 'between us'), then the sentence resumes or ends; or explicitly marks a digression ('By the way', 'A lyrical digression').
sentence_moves.not: Parentheses that only give a fact, a definition, an abbreviation, a citation or a list of examples.

sentence_moves.def: A sentence that voices a live reaction or a strong, unhedged evaluation: exclamation mark, oath, intensifier ('incredibly', 'terrifyingly', 'insane'), mock cheer.
sentence_moves.not: A mild evaluation at normal strength ('very slow', 'a good idea'); feelings named in a report (that is 'feeling_report').

sentence_moves.def: A short verbless or elliptical fragment set after a full sentence that intensifies or re-angles it ('Every day. Still.', 'Каждый день. До сих пор.', 'Not even close.').
sentence_moves.not: Fragments that announce what comes next (that is 'signpost'); one-word answers to the text's own question; headings.

sentence_moves.def: A word or phrase in quotation marks to mark it as someone else's label, trade jargon or irony ('so-called "best practices"', 'на «короткий чек»').
sentence_moves.not: Names of products, books, companies; direct speech.

sentence_moves.def: The writer stops an enumeration or explanation early on purpose and says so ('and so forth', 'I could go on', 'Long story short', 'and so on').
sentence_moves.not: A list that simply ends.

sentence_moves.def: A general claim told with a personal subject: the writer as the actor in a hypothetical or worked example ('Say I want to...'), or a generic 'you'/'we' that pulls the reader in, where an impersonal subject was available.
sentence_moves.not: 'We' meaning the writer's company or team doing real things; step-by-step instructions to the user.

text_moves.q: What does the first sentence (after any greeting or title) do?
text_moves.note: plain_setup = a neutral summary of the occasion, the topic, or the first fact stated plainly.

text_moves.q: What does the last sentence (before any sign-off) do?

text_moves.note: outside_forces = someone else's decision, pressure, accident, market or luck visibly shapes what happened.
marked_voice_held = the whole text keeps a slangy, mock-solemn, folksy-ironic or otherwise marked voice.

text_moves.q: Is one image or analogy carried through several paragraphs, gaining detail each time?

material.q: Does the writer hold an opinion of their own that someone could disagree with (beyond describing facts)?
How specific is the most concrete episode?
material.note: specific = one event with details only someone who was there would know.

material.q: Does a named or clearly identified other person (not the writer) do or say something in the text?
Does the writer admit a mistake, a doubt, a gap, or something that did not work?
Count concrete numbers and proper names (people, products, places, companies).
